subject: QuarterBind Order Form: pricing ladder, invoice routing & net terms
message_1_subject: QuarterBind proposed order form — pricing ladder & invoicing
message_1_body:
Markus —

Thanks for the call this week. Attached is our internal preferred redline of the Order Form (see attachment: QB_Proposed_OrderForm_redlines.pdf). High level asks from our side: 

- Move to Net30 for standard customers rather than Net45 (QuarterBind policy).
- Split invoices by entity: US entity for US consumption, EU entity for EU spend (we will provide VAT certs).
- Request an ‘accelerated commit’ credit if we ramp above 150% of the first-quarter commit in month 2 (details in redline).
- Escrow holdback: we want a small 3% holdback until onboarding acceptance for the first 30 days.

Can you review with finance and legal? We’re trying to close by end of next week; Lina (cc) will coordinate procurement paperwork on our side.

Thanks —
Nico
Nico Hernandez
Head of Procurement, QuarterBind
nico.hernandez@quarterbind.com
Attachment: QB_Proposed_OrderForm_redlines.pdf (pdf, 412KB)
message_2_subject: Re: QuarterBind proposed order form — pricing ladder & invoicing
message_2_body:
Nico — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. Quick responses while I loop legal/finance in: 

- Net terms: Our standard is Net45. We can offer Net30 on prepay or ACH with a small service-credit if we agree to faster payment terms (proposal: 1% service credit for Net30).
- Invoice split by entity: OK in principle; we need the VAT cert and the exact entity legal names and remit addresses before we can route invoices.
- Accelerated-commit credit: willing to discuss an acceleration credit tied to actual token usage; need to formalize the trigger and calculation (month vs quarter).
- Escrow holdback: 3% holdback for only the first invoice period is unusual for us — propose a 1% holdback limited to onboarding SLA breaches and capped to the first invoice only.

Cc’ing Kimberly for redlines to the Order Form and Ben in case accounts receivable needs to weigh in on the split-invoicing flow. I attached our initial comment file with line-item notes.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: please review the attached redline and propose MSA/Order Form language.
- Nico/Lina: please share VAT cert + remit details for EU entity.

Best,
Markus
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_initial_comments.docx (docx, 78KB)
message_3_subject: RE: QuarterBind proposed order form — legal redlines and tax evidence request
message_3_body:
Nico — I reviewed Markus’s notes and your redline. Summary of proposed legal positions from our side (high level):

1) Net terms / service credit
- We will accept Net30 only where QuarterBind prepays or executes ACH with cleared funds. Otherwise Net45 remains the default. Proposed contract language: "Net30 when payment received by electronic transfer; otherwise Net45; 1% service credit applies to invoices paid Net30 where pre-agreed."

2) Invoice entity split / tax evidence
- Redwood can emit separate invoices to two legal entities provided we receive: (a) formal entity names, (b) VAT registration certificate for EU entity, and (c) W-9 or equivalent for US entity. We will include standard tax-responsibility clause: "Taxes are the responsibility of the paying party based on their jurisdiction; withholding obligations remain with customer unless otherwise agreed in writing."

3) Accelerated-commit credit
- We need precise trigger language. Recommend: "If actual usage in any calendar month >= 150% of the pro rata monthly commit for the second calendar month post-activation, Customer receives X% credit applied to the subsequent invoice." Please confirm the % (we suggest 5% of incremental spend, capped at 20% of that month’s invoice).

4) Escrow/holdback
- Redwood cannot agree to open escrow. For onboarding protection we will agree to a 1% invoiced holdback tied to SLA failures with a maximum duration of 30 days and not cumulative across invoices.

I attached a clean redline with the exact proposed language and MSA cross-references (see attachment: OrderForm_Redline_20251009.docx). Also: legal needs QuarterBind’s legal entity registry extract AND a named billing contact for AR.

Next steps / timeline: 
- If QuarterBind agrees to the above, we can prepare a DocuSign order form and route to procurement by 10/14.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_Redline_20251009.docx (docx, 92KB)
message_4_subject: Re: QuarterBind Order Form: pricing ladder, invoice routing & net terms
message_4_body:
Markus / Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround. Quick responses from procurement/legal at QuarterBind: 

- Net terms: We can accept Net45 for card/credit, but we will provide ACH for the initial two invoices so Net30 (with your 1% service credit) is acceptable.
- VAT / entity docs: attached are the EU VAT cert (EU-VC-99122.pdf) and US W-9 (QB_US_W9.pdf). Legal registry and remit addresses included in attachment.
- Accelerated-commit credit: we accept the trigger language as proposed by Kimberly; QuarterBind prefers a 6% credit on incremental spend (rather than 5%). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept 6% capped at 20% of that month’s invoice?
- Escrow/holdback: QuarterBind is ok with 1% holdback tied to onboarding SLA for 30 days.

We’re prepared to proceed to DocuSign once language for the accelerated credit % is confirmed and you update the Order Form. Please send the DocuSign link when ready (we prefer a single combined Order Form/Signature page).

Thanks —
Lina Park
Senior Procurement Manager, QuarterBind
Attachments: EU-VC-99122.pdf (pdf, 34KB), QB_US_W9.pdf (pdf, 52KB), QuarterBind_entity_registry.zip (zip, 120KB)
